Joint B-spline functional Gaussian mixed-effects random slope

etr_fit_joint_bspline_functional_random_slope.Rd

Fits joint participant random-intercept and one random-slope functional B-spline model in native R using nlme. Participant random B-spline coefficients share an unstructured covariance; iid Gaussian residuals are assumed.

Usage

etr_fit_joint_bspline_functional_random_slope(
  trajectories, design, predictors, participant_column, dimension,
  random_slope_predictor, fixed_basis_size = 6L, random_basis_size = 4L,
  spline_degree = 3L, reml = TRUE, maxiter = 500L
)

Arguments

trajectories

Finite complete native trajectory collection.

design

Data frame containing a unique curve_id per source curve and numeric predictors.

predictors

Names of explicitly selected fixed scalar predictors.

participant_column

Participant identifier column in trajectory metadata.

dimension

Name of one measured response channel.

random_slope_predictor

Exactly one member of predictors; must vary within each participant.

fixed_basis_size

Number of clamped B-spline fixed-effect basis functions.

random_basis_size

Number of clamped B-spline functions per random intercept and random slope.

spline_degree

B-spline degree, from 1 to 5.

reml

Logical. TRUE performs REML; FALSE performs ML.

maxiter

Maximum nlme optimizer iterations.

Value

S3 etr_joint_bspline_mixed_slope inheriting from etr_joint_bspline_mixed, with fixed coefficient functions, SE, participant random intercept and slope functions, joint random covariance, residual variance, an IID residual_correlation_matrix equal to the time-grid identity matrix, fitted values, observed values and an nlme fit.

Details

This is an explicitly bounded native R implementation of the participant-only, one-slope, independent-residual scientific model. It does not claim full equivalence with the Python 1.2 statsmodels optimizer, error domain, typed results, nested random trial effects, or structured residual correlation. The participant count must exceed the number of free unstructured random-effect covariance parameters.
